assumptions: The premium escalation rule (CaseEscalationService.levelFor) changes; the Escalation_Level__c picklist values are unchanged.
Case.Escalation_Reason__c is excluded: it only feeds the comment body in recordEscalationReasons (CaseEscalationService.cls:71-82) and takes no part in choosing the level.

components.why: Defines who counts as a premium customer, so the rule change is checked against its values. It is one of the three seeds.
Holds the result of the rule; its picklist values stay as they are, so only its use is checked. It is a seed.
The open-hours threshold behind the Level 2 jump; the changed rule may read it differently. It is a seed.
Holds the escalation rule (levelFor), which is the change itself. It reads all three seed fields.
Asserts the levels for premium and standard cases, so its expectations must follow the new rule. It names Service_Level__c and Premium_SLA_Hours__c.
Should still pass unchanged: it goes through premiumCases, which filters only on Service_Level__c and never calls levelFor. It names Service_Level__c in setup, a hop-1 reader of the field.
Runs the trigger path end to end and asserts Escalation_Level__c, so it must still pass after the rule changes.
Hidden flow that fires when a case reaches Level 2, so it follows any change to when Level 2 is set. It filters on Escalation_Level__c and calls EscalationNotifier.
Rejects an escalated case without Level 1 or Level 2; with unchanged picklist values it should still hold, but it is checked.
Offers the Escalation_Level__c values to premium support cases; unchanged values mean no edit is expected.
Agents see the level and the escalation panel here. It shows Escalation_Level__c and hosts the panel, which a field search does not reach (the class-call chain does).
Agents must keep read access to the fields the rule uses. It grants the service level, escalation level and premium SLA fields, and the service class.
Team leads edit the escalation level and the premium SLA hours, so the rule change must respect that access. It grants those fields and the service class.
Account owners maintain Service_Level__c, so they decide who is premium under the new rule. It holds field permissions on two seed fields.

Hidden invocable that creates the owner's follow-up task for premium cases; it relies on CaseEscalationService.premiumCases. A field search misses it because it reads no field; only the class-call chain reaches it.
Dispatches case updates to the escalation service, so a signature change would break it. Shared with the assignment story DEMO-202; reached through CaseEscalationService.

Agents read the premium label, level and SLA state here; its state comes from getEscalationState, so a levelFor-only change needs no edit but the display is checked. A field search misses it; only the class-call chain reaches it.
Entry point for the whole chain; unaffected unless handler contexts change. A field search misses it; only the class-call chain reaches it.
